articles.title: Let’s All Be Happy This AAA Minesweeper Game Isn’t Real
articles.summary: Minesweeper has been around for decades and it's probably overdue for some modern flourishes. Now there's a Triple-A Minesweeper parody that offers a hilarious look at what a Minesweeper update might look like.
body: The Triple-A Minesweeper was created by writer and programmer Mike Lacher, and it's fully playable as a browser game on his site. Aside from the intentionally pretentious title cards touting the involvement of Unreal Engine, Nvidia, Bink Video, and Wwise, Triple A Minesweeper looks and plays almost exactly like the regular Minesweeper.

However, the best way to enjoy this parody is by simply not doing anything at all. The main character, "Sweeper," will sit around and repeat things like, "I gotta sweep these mines," while receiving calls from newly created characters in the game. Lacher seems to have taken his inspiration from Grand Theft Auto 5, Metal Gear Solid, and even Cyberpunk 2077.

Among the callers are Nora, a potential love interest for Sweeper. Additionally, an underworld figure called The Don repeatedly calls for Sweeper to head down to his club while hinting at the latter's sinister past in Singapore. Meanwhile, the chipper DJ Dan celebrates Sweeper's efforts on behalf of New Dawn City.
points: Minesweeper has been around for decades and it's probably overdue for some modern flourishes.
Now there's a Triple-A Minesweeper parody that offers a hilarious look at what a Minesweeper update might look like.

articles.title: Konami Planning 'Second and Third Waves' of New Silent Hill Games
articles.summary: Konami is planning "second and third waves" of new Silent Hill games, according to producer Motoi Okamoto. Okamoto offered a foggy glimpse into the classic horror franchise's future during an interview featured in Famitsu Issue 1965 (via Game Observer ).
body: "All three titles we initially announced were able to be released successfully, so we’re relieved (laughs)," he noted. "They’ve also received high praise, and we are satisfied with it."

Okamoto continued: "Successfully launching this 'first wave' comes with great relief, but we’re not stopping here; we must think of the second and third waves. We can’t share specific details, but we’re currently looking at a number of projects."

The first wave of Konami's return to Silent Hill – which included titles like the Silent Hill 2 remake, Silent Hill f, and last month's Silent Hill: Townfall – rolled out throughout the last few years. Townfall arrived as the most recent installment when it dropped players into the shoes of protagonist Simon Ordell in a '90s Scotland just last month.

It received generally favorable reviews, with IGN giving it an 8/10. We said, "Like the intravenous needle permanently jutting out of its hero’s wrist, Silent Hill: Townfall gives this long running series a welcome shot in the arm."

articles.title: Blumhouse Partners With MatPat to Make Amanda the Adventurer Movie, Confirms More Indie Horror Game Adaptations Are Coming | NYCC 2026
articles.summary: Blumhouse Productions has partnered with YouTube star Matthew ‘MatPat’ Patrick to create a series of movies based on viral indie horror games, and Amanda the Adventurer is first on the docket.
body: Representatives from Blumhouse and MatPat confirmed this partnership at New York Comic Con 2026, where they said the YouTuber has “a few projects in the works” with the studio.

“I am proud to announce that I’m working with Blumhouse to launch some new movies. I am taking some of my all-time favorite indie games and horror channels from the interwebs and partnering with Blumhouse to bring them to the big screen,” MatPat said at the panel.

The first of these is Amanda the Adventurer, a first-person, puzzle-solving indie horror game that sees the player character unravel an unsettling mystery involving a low-budget animated children’s show of the same name.
MatPat announced that he and Blumhouse are currently in talks with writers and directors, saying they’re “actually moving fast” to get this project made.

articles.title: Call Of Duty: MW4 Early Access Also Includes DMZ, Here’s How To Get In
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's campaign is playable a week early for people who preorder, and now we know the DMZ mode will be as well. Activision has announced that MW4's extraction-based DMZ mode will be playable starting Tuesday, October 20, which is three days before the game launches.
body: To access DMZ mode before everyone else, you need to preorder any edition of MW4, including the standard or Vault versions. The perk applies to all platforms: PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, and PC.

Described as the "definitive extraction shooter experience," DMZ in MW4 is an open-world game mode featuring other human players and AI combatants. Players will search the map for loot, craft gear, and complete objectives. Like in other extraction-based games, you need to reach the exfil point to make it out with all your rewards.

DMZ originally debuted with 2022's MW3 as a free-to-play beta inside Warzone, but this version left a lot to be desired. The new version of DMZ for MW4 seems like a big step up, and it includes a new social space this time as well.
For lots more, be sure to read up on GameSpot's previous coverage of the new version of DMZ.

articles.title: Is The Exorcist: Martyrs a Sequel to The Exorcist III? Mike Flanagan Reveals All
articles.summary: The Exorcist: Martyrs director Mike Flanagan joins IGN to break down the horror sequel's new trailer and explain how it builds on the foundation of The Exorcist III.
body: There's a lot to be excited about at this year's NYCC, not least of which being the first trailer for Mike Flanagan's The Exorcist: Martyrs. The previous attempt at reinvigorating this iconic horror franchise didn't go so well, but if anyone can turn the ship around, it's the man behind The Haunting of Hill House and the new Carrie series.

IGN's Tom Jorgensen was able to sit down with Flanagan and take a deep dive into the trailer. Flanagan breaks down the key characters seen in this new footage and how the film builds on the foundation of the underrated gem that is The Exorcist III. Check out our video interview above or read on to see what he had to say about the film, including the all-important question of whether or not we'll hear "Tubular Bells" in the new film.

Tom Jorgensen for IGN: [Let's start with] the first shot of the trailer, which is Scarlett [Johansson] coming down the stairs into that crime scene. Explain why that was the image that you wanted to come right out of the gate with for this trailer.

articles.title: A Street Fighter Movie Sequel Is Already Being Written, but There’s a Catch
articles.summary: Director Kitao Sakurai confirmed that he’s already hard at work writing up a sequel to his upcoming Street Fighter film, but whether or not it gets made all depends on how the first movie performs.
body: Sakurai spoke about the possibility of a sequel in an interview with MovieWeb, saying the groundwork is already being laid to continue Ryu and Ken’s adventures after the events of the second World Warrior Tournament. But if fans want to see their fights continue after this, they’ll have to put their butts in some seats at their local theaters to make it happen.

“It's something that we're thinking about and developing,” he told the outlet. “I don't want to say anything that locks us in. It also kind of depends on how people react to this one, and whether they, you know, support this vision of the story. We definitely have a lot of ideas, and we're writing currently, but you know, I wouldn't want to make any promises one way or the other about what exactly we're gonna do."

Having spoken with the cast myself, I can confirm that their hopes for a sequel are high, but they’ve also confirmed that interest from moviegoers is essential in order to justify making another Street Fighter film.
points: Director Kitao Sakurai confirmed that he’s already hard at work writing up a sequel to his upcoming Street Fighter film, but whether or not it gets made all depends on how the first movie performs.

articles.title: Gears Of War: E-Day–How’s It Selling? Let’s Unpack Things
articles.summary: Microsoft's latest console exclusive, Gears of War: E-Day, launched this week, and now we've gotten the first glimpse at how the game is performing commercially. Multiple analysts have weighed in, and there are numerous factors at play beyond pure sales, due to Game Pass and other factors.
body: Rhys Elliott of Alinea Analytics released a report that said the game has sold about 230,000 copies so far, with Steam sales accounting for 168,000 and Xbox (across console and PC) making up the other 62,000.

Straight sales do not tell the whole story, though, because E-Day is available on Game Pass, which Elliott said "cannibalized" the majority of sales. He said Alinea's data showed than 1.7 million people acquired E-Day through their Game Pass subscription as opposed to buying a copy outright.

There is more nuance there, too, as Elliott said that 722,000 of the 1.7 million people who played E-Day through Game Pass bought the $30 Premium upgrade, which got them in early and awarded them with extra content.

"So despite selling far fewer copies on Steam, Xbox accounts for almost three-quarters of the revenue (roughly $26 million of the $37 million, versus about $11 million on Steam). So '230,000 copies' undersells the paying audience. Including the 722,000 upgrades, nearly 950,000 people actually paid something for E-Day."

articles.title: 5 Hilarious 'Calvin and Hobbes' Comic Strips About Hating School
articles.summary: Calvin and Hobbes took a different approach. What set Calvin apart from most of his funny-pages peers, with the exceptions of Huey and Riley Freeman, was that school might've been the most uncomplicated villain in C&H canon.
body: There are plenty of comic strips about kids who have an adversarial relationship with school. Peanuts features both Sally Brown and Peppermint Patty, and early Bloom County was often set in a classroom where the teachers were not at all ready for the Michael Binkley experience. On the other end of the scale, Jason Fox is so good at school that he usually wrecks the experience for everyone else.

That, in turn, is arguably a big part of what made Calvin and Hobbes an instant classic during its original newspaper run. Because of Bill Watterson's love of vocabulary, Calvin was always shown as being much smarter than the average six-year-old, even if that was just because it was funny to put graduate-level verbiage in a first-grader's mouth. He was just a poor fit for public school. If you're anywhere near Calvin's age, or just honestly remember that time in your life, it's easy to see your own school years reflected in him.

School is a big focus of Calvin and Hobbes, so a full rundown of all the strips on the subject would take up a book by itself. Instead, here are five strips chosen as some of the highlights of Calvin's ongoing struggles with the traditional education system.

articles.title: Square Enix's Forgotten Loot-Shooter Was Years Ahead of Its Time
articles.summary: Some of the most-discussed multiplayer shooter of 2026 share a lot in common. In both Arc Raiders and Marathon, you and up to two other players venture from a safe hub into hostile areas, shoot a bunch of enemies, grab a bunch of loot, and return back to safety.
body: People Can Fly’s Outriders, published by Square Enix and released on April 1, 2021 (not a joke!), wasn’t an extraction shooter, but it hit many of the same beats. You and up to two other players decamped from a hub city, venturing into hostile areas where you’d shoot a bunch of enemies and grab a bunch of loot before returning back to safety to sift through that loot, at which point you’d fine-tune your builds to do it all again. Again, Outriders was not an extraction shooter — the stakes were lower, for one, and it didn’t feature PvP — but the feedback loop scratched a similar itch as the shooters du jour.

articles.title: Battlefield 6 Is Adding Something Fans Have Wanted Since Day 1
articles.summary: EA and Battlefield Studios have unveiled more details on Battlefield 6 's upcoming Season 5, and it includes a new feature that fans have wanted since day one: a proper server browser.
body: Battlefield did indeed launch with a server browser, but--considering how it only supported Portal mode--it wasn't the one fans wanted. One of the game's producers asked why players even want a full server browser. Now, in response to the feedback, Battlefield Studios is adding a proper server browser with the Season 5 update this December, allowing people to create their own servers and set rules like map rotation and other particulars. Classic-era Battlefield games had server browsers, and fans flocked to them because they could pick and choose exactly the maps and modes they wanted to play.

Season 5 rolls out in waves, beginning with Siege of Las Vegas on October 13, which adds two new maps: Vegas Strip and Area 51. For Battlefield 6's battle royale RedSec, Siege of Las Vegas adds a new version of the mode called Rapid Royale, which promises faster rounds with smaller player populations.

articles.title: GTA 6's Nudity Sure Sounds Hopelessly Outdated
articles.summary: More GTA 6 leaks are spilling out, despite Rockstar's best efforts, and one of the bigger ones seems to be Jason's penis. Well, I haven't seen the video as it's been taken down, so I don't know how big that particular leak is.
body: In a city no stranger to sex and nudity, playing GTA 6 with either or both characters entirely in the buff for as long as you want to is not an event. It's childish, really, a shallow take on sexuality that equates bodies with excitement just for the sake of it.

Official GTA 6 materials prior to the most recent leak mentioned something about potentially cutting back to Jason, for example, while he's in the shower. That sounds sexy, an unexpected glimpse at a quiet, intimate moment that's entirely outside your control, and then you go back to normalcy after it ends. That's sexy! Heck, it'd be sexy even if the scene didn't show Jason (or Lucia) entirely nude. Controlled, consensual reveals where the process is just as exciting as the result are inherently much sexier than just full dong or whatever.

articles.title: Steven Spielberg's 145-Minute 2026 Sci-fi Thriller Now Officially Streaming
articles.summary: Steven Spielberg has spent much of his career looking to the stars. From the wonder of Close Encounters of the Third Kind to the childhood adventure of E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, few filmmakers have done more to shape the way Hollywood approaches stories about humanity making contact with…
body: Now, Spielberg's latest alien movie has finally made the jump from theaters to streaming.

Disclosure Day began streaming exclusively on Peacock on Friday, Oct. 9, giving Spielberg fans a new opportunity to catch the director's latest exploration of alien conspiracies. The sci-fi epic arrived in theaters on June 12, where it earned mostly favorable reviews and became one of the more prominent releases of the summer. The movie earned a respectable $244 million at the global box office.
Disclosure Day follows several people who find themselves caught up in a decades-old conspiracy surrounding humanity's encounters with extraterrestrial life.

Josh O'Connor plays Daniel Kellner, a cybersecurity expert who steals information from the powerful corporation Wardex, revealing an almost 80-year-old government cover-up involving alien visitations. He soon finds himself on the run from Wardex agents determined to recover the information before it can reach the public.

body: This comes just days after modding platform ReSkate blew up big time, reaching 350,000 downloads in mere hours. ReSkate essentially lets players experience the skating sim revival completely offline, unlike the online-only base game, with custom maps and cosmetics and servers.

"Like many of you, we've been following the launch of numerous mods for our game. Skateboarding in general is built on community and creative expression, and we support that. We love seeing your passion for pushing the limits of San Vansterdam in different ways. That’s why we built our new skateboarding sandbox in San Vansterdam to begin with, to give you, the players, the tools you need to have fun and create amazing content," a developer statement posted to Reddit and other online forums said.

articles.title: As Xbox and PlayStation sales reach new lows, analyst says the "US hardware market has not been in a more precarious position since the early 80s"
articles.summary: PS5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles are more expensive than ever in most markets, thanks largely to memory components being gobbled up by AI data centres. Now, analyst Mat Piscatella worries the console market, at least in the US, hasn't looked this dire since the early 1980s, which was maybe…
body: Circana's Piscatella recently jumped online to reveal that Xbox and PS5 price hikes caused a big blow to sales, somewhat unsurprisingly. Xbox hardware sales are reportedly down 33% "versus a year ago in the US, while PlayStation hardware units are 25% lower." Those year-to-date stats mark a new all-time low for Xbox, and PlayStation's lowest point since 2013.

"The average price a consumer has paid for a new Xbox console in 2026 YTD ending August is $529, 26% higher than a year ago, while the average PlayStation console has sold for $597, 20% higher than last year," Piscatella added. "Both prices are at all-time US highs. Price sensitivity is becoming a real problem."

There's been some hope the incoming and meteoric launch of GTA 6 next month could give both consoles a boost, and Piscatella also noted that Rockstar's mammoth might "help ease at least some of these declines," but that's all dependent on pricing and "product availability." If all the RAM is booked for AI data centres, Microsoft and Sony won't be able to make as many consoles as they can sell.
"The US hardware market has not been in a more precarious position since the early 80s," Piscatella added.
points: PS5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles are more expensive than ever in most markets, thanks largely to memory components being gobbled up by AI data centres.

articles.title: Cyberpunk 2077 is being made into a movie, even though we've already got the perfect cyberpunk movie starring Keanu Reeves as a guy named Johnny
articles.summary: X A Deadline report says Paramount Pictures is working with CD Projekt Red on a live-action movie set in the Cyberpunk 2077 universe, with Lorenzo di Bonaventura, whose previous films include a pile of Transformers movies, a couple GI Joe flicks, and the 2005 Doom movie starring The Rock, attached…
body: There's really no more detail at this point, so instead of talking about that I'm going to take a hard swerve and remind everyone that the perfect cyberpunk movie already exists, and it even stars Johnny Silverhand himself, Keanu Reeves—as another guy named Johnny who's having a rough time in the cyber-future, believe it or not.

Johnny (Mnemonic, not Silverhand) takes on a high-risk, high-reward mission, which naturally goes south almost immediately: He's hunted by the yakuza, betrayed by his handler, rescued by a sexy cyborg, gets his ass beat by a preacher, is saved by a dolphin, and ultimately destroys capitalism. Something like that, anyway—it's been a while.

Okay, look, it might seem silly now, but trust me, in 1995 this was a goddamn who's-who of people who were cool and not too expensive in 1995. And while the film was, uh, not particularly well received (but it did make money!), I dug it. I was baffled by the dolphin thing and had no idea what the hell Dolph Lundgren was even doing there, but I distinctly recall leaving the theater thinking, that was fun!

videos.title: Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves x Tekken 8 - Official Reina Teaser Trailer
videos.summary: Check out the Tekken 8 Reina Teaser Trailer for Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves, the hit fighting game developed by SNK. Players can get a look at Reina, also referred to as Purple Lightning, making her debut with the upcoming Tekken 8 collaboration.
points: Check out the Tekken 8 Reina Teaser Trailer for Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves, the hit fighting game developed by SNK.
Players can get a look at Reina, also referred to as Purple Lightning, making her debut with the upcoming Tekken 8 collaboration.
Reina is launching into Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves in December 2026 for PlayStation 4 (PS4), PlayStation 5 (PS5), Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC (Steam and Epic Games Store).
videos.author: IGN

videos.title: Forever Ago – Launch Trailer – Nintendo Switch 2
videos.summary: Play Forever Ago now on Nintendo Switch 2:
body: Following a tragic stroke of fate, Alfred embarks on a journey north in search of redemption. In this single-player road trip adventure, you'll travel to beautiful places, capture memories with your camera, meet interesting characters, and even make some new friends.
